headline: Record quarter, margins expand, guidance raised again
summary_short: Revenue rose 10.3% y/y to $1,695.7M and diluted EPS climbed 34.7% to $0.97, as SS&C raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.93-$7.25.
summary_long: Revenue rose 10.3% y/y to $1,695.7M on $117.6M of organic growth (GlobeOp fund administration, Wealth and Investment Technology, Global Investor and Distribution Solutions), plus $35.9M from acquisitions and $5.4M FX. Gross margin expanded 30bp to 48.3% as cost of revenues grew slower (+9.7%) than revenue. Opex rose just 2.2% (organic opex fell on lower personnel costs), lifting operating income 21.1% to $417.1M. Net income climbed 29.9% to $234.8M; diluted EPS rose to $0.97 from $0.72. SS&C raised FY2026 guidance to $6,672-$6,832M revenue and $6.93-$7.25 adjusted EPS (up from April's $6,664-$6,824M / $6.74-$7.06). It repurchased $605.7M of stock, paid $0.27/share dividends, while cash fell to $434.8M and long-term debt rose 7.5% to $7,312.2M.

drivers.explanation: Organic growth of $117.6M (GlobeOp fund administration, Wealth and Investment Technology, Global Investor and Distribution Solutions) plus $35.9M from acquisitions and $5.4M FX tailwind.
Reflects $54.5M of organic cost increase (continued investment in client service) plus $20.2M from acquisitions and $2.8M unfavorable FX.
Revenue growth (+10.3%) outpaced cost-of-revenue growth (+9.7%) and total opex growth of just 2.2%, since organic opex actually fell $7.9M on lower personnel costs.

Net income and EPS growth reflect margin expansion and a lower share count from buybacks (242.0M diluted shares vs 252.2M a year ago), partly offset by higher interest expense ($107.0M vs $105.5M) and a higher effective tax rate (25.1% vs 24.4%).
$605.7M of share repurchases, $129.3M of dividends, and other financing/investing outflows more than offset $716.4M of six-month operating cash flow.
Equity declined as $605.7M of buybacks and $129.3M of dividends paid out exceeded retained net income growth over the trailing year.
